scope: Two app-owned slots, fixed copy and terminal-first paired collection

review.scope: p001-full-return-transport-v1: Source-only review of the new fixed private return reservation/copy/collection module and tests. Existing source-reviewed full206-member local intake and frozen validation are unchanged. 80 combined tests passed including28new; actual frozen selection metadata produced exact206-member set. Existing persistent Drive OAuth/drive.file/output folder grant is approved and installed; no new consent or patient transfer authority inferred. This module uses protected API client to reserve only two app-owned nonempty marker slots, checks exact parent/ownership/IDs/readback, proposes aliases without installing them, emits CPU and fixed copy cells and collects terminal before ZIP through existing DriveEvidence. It requires existing private folder, exact pins/runtime and stopped processes; patient branch requires VALIDATED worker status/parameter hash and separate canary receipt and launch manifest bindings. It performs bounded exact206-member ZIP metadata check BEFORE patient copy, combined32MiB receipt+ZIP cap, explicit operational expansion cap, in-place existing-slot replacement, original-byte preservation, exclusive intent and no retry after uncertainty. Synthetic pair is separate harmless ZIP. Actual native Colab source/readback/protocol verification and protected installation wrapper are still separate required integration work, not claimed here. Collection establishes original Drive IDs/bytes, never OS exit or scientific acceptance; unchanged frozen validator runs later. Review concrete remaining command-generation correctness, dependency imports, private paths, cap and role scope, metadata identity/races, original preservation and recovery risks. No general adapter redesign or duplicate prior validation requested.
findings: No blockers. Reservation binds nonce-derived marker content, exact names/IDs/parent/ownedByMe/owner-only permissions with size+md5 and byte-for-byte readback through the protected client; aliases are only proposed (config untouched, verified by test); slot Drive IDs and output_folder_id never appear in the copy packet or cells; binding_sha256 recomputation in validate_reservation covers request_id/purpose/nonce/parent_id/slots so any slot or parent substitution invalidates the receipt.

Command/cell generation is correct: the cell prelude imports stat/struct/zipfile/PurePosixPath and pins MEMBER_COUNT/DIRECTORY_CAP/AGGREGATES, and runtime_observation/check_directory/inspect_members/runtime_member_names/copy_return each import their remaining dependencies inside the function body, so the generated namespace is closed (traced name-by-name; compile() alone would not catch NameError). verify_packet exactness holds because prepare_copy is deterministic given pins (fixed-date synthetic ZIP, insertion-ordered repr, git-pinned runtime packet).

Ordering and caps hold: the exact-206 check_directory + inspect_members admission runs on the already-open source handle BEFORE the intent file or any slot write; the combined receipt+ZIP <= 32 MiB check precedes slot opens; collection re-derives sizes from pre-download metadata, refuses before either download on overflow, collects terminal first, then narrows the zip alias max_bytes to min(terminal-declared zip_bytes, remaining cap) in a deep-copied scoped registry, and cross-checks collected zip sha256/bytes against the terminal plus before/after slot metadata including parents/ownership.

Preservation and no-retry semantics are sound: patient source ZIP is opened read-only with O_NOFOLLOW and fstat/lstat identity capture, then rechecked (handle identity, path lstat identity, full re-hash, and worker_status re-read) after the ZIP copy but before the terminal receipt — the last slot write; intent is O_EXCL-created, fsynced with parent-directory fsync, and a pre-existing intent or consumed marker blocks retry (marker gate fires first after success, FileExistsError after interruption); reserve_slots persists binding before ID allocation and never re-allocates after an uncertain failure.

Minor diagnostics: the fixed cell's exception wrapper only passes codes matching P001_COPY_[A-Z_]+, so check_directory/inspect_members failures (P001_RETURN_ZIP_DIRECTORY, P001_RETURN_MEMBER_SET, P001_RETURN_EXPANSION_CAP, etc.) surface from the remote cell only as the generic P001_COPY_FAILED_PRESERVE_PRIVATE_STATE. Fail-closed and payload-free, but it hides the most reconciliation-relevant pre-copy admission cause; consider widening the regex to P001_(COPY|RETURN)_[A-Z_]+ (all such codes are fixed strings).

Minor recovery asymmetry: collect_pair returns BLOCKED_RECONCILE for any existing collection directory, including one holding a successful receipt.json, unlike reserve_slots which replays a verified prior receipt; a repeated status query therefore looks like a failure and forces manual inspection. Also, reserve_slots's recovery branch (read_json + validate_reservation of the old receipt) sits outside the try/except, so a truncated or corrupted receipt raises KeyError/JSONDecodeError to the caller instead of the module's structured BLOCKED_RECONCILE — fail-closed but inconsistent stop semantics.

Cap/role scope note: the installed zip alias carries max_bytes = TRANSFER_CAP, so a direct broker collect outside collect_pair could transfer up to 32 MiB + RECEIPT_CAP combined (16 KiB over the combined ceiling) and skips the terminal-first identity check; collect_pair itself enforces the combined cap. Negligible margin and operator-only route, but worth remembering that the combined-cap guarantee lives in collect_pair, not in the registry entry.

Namespace edge: request_identity accepts collection request_ids beginning with 'upload-' (and reserve request_ids likewise), which DriveEvidence reserves for its store path; such an id fails only inside the try after the intent/collection directory is created, leaving a blocked directory to reconcile. Cosmetic — an early refusal would be cleaner.

Metadata identity/race note (untested here, for the native canary): identity() includes st_mtime_ns/st_ctime_ns on Drive FUSE paths, so a FUSE metadata refresh between open and the post-copy recheck could spuriously raise P001_COPY_SOURCE_OR_STATUS_CHANGED or SLOT_PATH_REPLACED; similarly modifiedTime/version in slot_metadata before/after comparisons may be sensitive to backend metadata churn during collection. All failure modes are fail-closed BLOCKED_RECONCILE, but expect possible false stops on the real mount — exactly what the synthetic canary should measure.

Authority bindings are bindings only, as scoped: worker_parameters_sha256 is actually enforced against worker bytes in the patient cell, but canary_receipt_sha256 and launch_manifest_sha256 are caller-supplied hashes bound into the packet and terminal without content verification in this module — the separate launch-decision/installation wrapper must verify them before invoking the patient branch. os.umask(0o077) in copy_return mutates process-global state without restore (same note as the intake review; harmless in the single-purpose cell).

Test source note (no execution claimed): the 28 new cases (21 functions, 10 parametrized instances) cover reservation idempotence/no-reallocation, wrong parent/ownership/permissions, uncertain-create preservation, packet exactness and ID absence, marker/intent refusal without overwrite, combined-cap-before-write, partial-write interruption, replaced-source-before-terminal, FUSE-ID-replacement detection, extra-member refusal, collection cap/terminal-first ordering, and direct execution of the generated cell namespace for both purposes. Remaining gaps match the declared separate integration work: runtime_member_names is exercised only with a mocked subprocess and monkeypatched in copy tests, DriveEvidence is driven with a FakeDrive rather than the native client, and alias installation, launch-manifest verification and the actual Colab readback/protocol canary are not claimed by this module.

tests: 80 focused tests including28 new transport cases
